headline: Android Photo Picker to get new API for explicit location data sharing
summary: Google is updating Android's default image selection interface to give users explicit control over sharing location data embedded in photos and videos.
details: Google is rolling out a new API for Android developers that will allow users to choose whether to share location data embedded in photos and videos when using the Android Photo Picker. This update aims to provide greater user control over personal data.

The updated Photo Picker will present users with an option to share location information, and their selection will be saved for future use. Additionally, there will be a clear option to remove location access entirely, giving users the power to toggle this setting on or off.

This enhancement is part of a larger effort to improve user privacy and data control within the Android ecosystem. While this is the first step, Google may introduce further updates in the future to refine these privacy features.

The new API is slated to go live with the "August 2026 Mainline update," according to a Reddit thread. This timeline suggests that the feature will be integrated into a future core Android update, making it available to a wide range of devices.
